questions.text: कान्हा, रेशम तथा निशा एक फ़र्म के साझेदार थे। निशा ने फ़र्म को 10% वार्षिक दर से ₹ 1,00,000 का ऋण दिया था। फ़र्म का लेखापाल ऋण पर 6% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज देने के लिए जोर दे रहा है। निशा को किस दर से ऋण पर ब्याज दिया जाएगा ?
questions.text_english: Kanha, Resham and Nisha were partners in a firm. Nisha had given a loan of ₹ 1,00,000 to the firm @ 10% p.a. The accountant of the firm is emphasizing that interest on loan will be paid @ 6% p.a. At what rate the interest on loan will be paid to Nisha?

options.D: ऋण पर कोई ब्याज नहीं दिया जाएगा ।

options_english.D: No interest on loan will be paid.

questions.solution: The interest on the loan will be paid to Nisha at the explicitly agreed upon rate of 10% per annum. The statutory provision of 6% per annum under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 applies only in the absence of an agreement, but here a specific rate of 10% was already established when the loan was given.
questions.topic: Interest on Partner's Loan to the Firm

questions.text: गुप्ता तथा शर्मा एक फ़र्म के साझेदार हैं तथा 4:1 के अनुपात में लाभ बाँटते हैं। उन्होंने लाभों में 1/4 भाग के लिए प्रीति को एक नया साझेदार बनाया, जिसे उसने पूर्णतः गुप्ता से प्राप्त किया। गुप्ता, शर्मा तथा प्रीति का नया लाभ विभाजन अनुपात होगा :
questions.text_english: Gupta and Sharma are partners in a firm sharing profit in the ratio of 4:1. They admitted Preeti as a new partner for 1/4th share in the profits, which she acquired wholly from Gupta. New profit sharing ratio of Gupta, Sharma and Preeti will be:
questions.solution: Option B is correct because Preeti acquires her entire 1/4th share strictly from Gupta. Gupta's original share was 4/5. Subtracting Preeti's share (1/4) from Gupta's share yields (16-5)/20 = 11/20. Sharma's share remains unchanged at 1/5, which is equivalent to 4/20. Preeti's share is 1/4, which is equivalent to 5/20. Therefore, the new profit sharing ratio seamlessly becomes 11:4:5.

questions.text: आदित्य, विशेष तथा निमेष एक फ़र्म के साझेदार थे तथा लाभ-हानि बराबर-बराबर बाँटते थे । 1 जुलाई, 2023 को आदित्य की मृत्यु हो गई। शेष साझेदारों ने फ़र्म का व्यवसाय चालू रखने का निर्णय किया तथा भविष्य में लाभों को 4:3 के अनुपात में बाँटने का निर्णय लिया। विशेष तथा निमेष का अधिलाभ अनुपात होगा :
questions.text_english: Aditya, Vishesh and Nimesh were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses equally. Aditya died on 1st July, 2023. Remaining partners decided to continue the business of the firm and decided to share future profits in the ratio of 4:3. The gaining ratio of Vishesh and Nimesh will be :
questions.solution: Option C is correct because the gaining ratio is calculated by subtracting the old share from the new share. Vishesh's gain is 4/7 minus 1/3, which mathematically simplifies to (12-7)/21 = 5/21. Nimesh's gain is 3/7 minus 1/3, which simplifies to (9-7)/21 = 2/21. Thus, the gaining ratio precisely evaluates to 5:2.

sub_questions.text_english: Vishant Ltd. invited applications for issuing 6,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each at 10% premium. The issue was fully subscribed. The amount per share was payable as follows: On application ₹ 3, on allotment ₹ 3 (including premium), on first call ₹ 3 and on final call ₹ 2. Ashish the holder of 200 shares paid the entire money along with allotment. The total amount received on allotment was:
sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct because the standard allotment money due for all 6,000 shares is calculated as 6,000 multiplied by ₹ 3, which equals ₹ 18,000. Additionally, Ashish paid his first and final call money in advance on his 200 shares. The advance amount is 200 multiplied by the sum of both calls (₹ 3 + ₹ 2 = ₹ 5), yielding ₹ 1,000. Therefore, the total cash received exactly amounts to ₹ 18,000 plus ₹ 1,000, bringing it to ₹ 19,000.

sub_questions.text: एम लिमिटेड ने ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 5,000 समता अंशों/शेयरों का, जिन्हें 10% प्रीमियम पर निर्गमित किया गया था, ₹2 प्रति अंश/शेयर की अन्तिम याचना का भुगतान नहीं करने पर हरण (Forfeit) कर लिया। वह न्यूनतम राशि जिस पर इन अंशों/शेयरों को पूर्ण प्रदत्त पुनः निर्गमित किया जा सकता है, होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: M Ltd. forfeited 5,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each issued at a premium of 10% for non-payment of final call of ₹ 2 per share. The minimum amount at which these shares can be reissued as fully paid up will be:
sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct because the maximum permissible discount on the reissue of forfeited shares is strictly equal to the amount already received towards the share capital on those shares. Here, out of the ₹ 10 face value, ₹ 2 remains unpaid, meaning ₹ 8 per share has been successfully collected. Hence, the maximum discount allowed is ₹ 8 per share. Consequently, the minimum price at which a share can be reissued as fully paid-up is the remaining ₹ 2 per share. For 5,000 shares, the total minimum reissue amount mathematically evaluates to 5,000 multiplied by ₹ 2, which is ₹ 10,000.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : स्थायी पूँजी विधि के अन्तर्गत, साझेदारों के पूँजी खाते सदैव ज़मा शेष दर्शाते हैं।

निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Under the fixed capital method, partners' capital accounts always show a credit balance.
Reason (R): Under the fixed capital method, all items like share of profit or loss, interest on capital, drawings, interest on drawings are recorded in a separate account called partners' current account.
Choose the correct alternative from the following:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, लेकिन कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, लेकिन कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is incorrect.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is incorrect, but Reason (R) is correct.

questions.solution: Option A is correct because under the fixed capital method, the principal capital balance remains completely unchanged unless additional capital is formally introduced or permanently withdrawn, ensuring it consistently maintains a credit balance. The Reason perfectly explains this phenomenon by correctly outlining that all regular profit appropriations, drawings, and interest calculations are exclusively diverted to a separate current account, thereby legally protecting the main capital account from routine fluctuations.

sub_questions.text_english: Vanya and Aanya were partners in a firm sharing profit and losses in the ratio of 3:2. Their capital were ₹ 5,00,000 and ₹ 1,00,000 respectively. Vanya was entitled to interest on capital @ 8% p.a. and Aanya was entitled to salary @ ₹ 5,000 per month. The net profit before any appropriation was ₹ 1,75,000. Vanya's share in divisible profit will be:
sub_questions.solution: Option A is correct because the total appropriations need to be calculated first. Vanya's interest on capital is evaluated as 8% of ₹ 5,00,000, which strictly amounts to ₹ 40,000. Aanya's annual salary calculates to ₹ 5,000 multiplied by 12 months, equaling ₹ 60,000. Summing these provides total appropriations of ₹ 1,00,000. Subtracting this from the net profit of ₹ 1,75,000 leaves exactly ₹ 75,000 as the final divisible profit. Vanya's share is 3/5th of this ₹ 75,000, which flawlessly results in ₹ 45,000.

sub_questions.text: ओंकार तथा शिवा एक फ़र्म के साझेदार थे। ओंकार ₹ 20,000 वार्षिक वेतन का अधिकारी था; जबकि शिवा ₹ 50,000 वार्षिक वेतन का अधिकारी था। ओंकार और शिवा का वेतन प्रभारित करने के बाद 31 मार्च, 2023 को समाप्त होने वाले वर्ष का शुद्ध लाभ ₹ 5,60,000 था । ओंकार के पूँजी खाते में जमा की जाने वाली कुल राशि होगी :

Net profit for the year ended 31st March, 2023 after charging salary of Omkar and Shiva was ₹ 5,60,000. The total amount credited to Omkar's capital account will be:
sub_questions.solution: Option D is correct because the given net profit of ₹ 5,60,000 is explicitly stated to be after charging the salaries. This signifies that ₹ 5,60,000 is the final divisible profit. Since no specific profit-sharing ratio is mentioned in the problem, the Partnership Act mandates an equal distribution. Omkar receives exactly half of the divisible profit, amounting to ₹ 2,80,000. To find the total amount credited to his capital account, his dedicated salary of ₹ 20,000 is added to his profit share, yielding an accurate final total of ₹ 3,00,000.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : वाहक ऋणपत्रों पर ब्याज का भुगतान उस व्यक्ति को किया जाता है जो इस प्रकार के ऋणपत्रों में संलग्न ब्याज कूपन को प्रस्तुत करते हैं।

निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Interest on bearer debentures is paid to a person who produces the interest coupon attached to such debentures.
Reason (R): Bearer debentures are transferred by way of delivery and the company does not keep any record of these debenture holders.
Choose the correct option from the following:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, लेकिन कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, लेकिन कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is incorrect.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is incorrect, but Reason (R) is correct.

questions.solution: Option A is correct because both statements represent fundamental factual mechanisms of corporate finance. Assertion (A) accurately states that bearer debenture interest requires physical coupon presentation. Reason (R) is fully accurate and supplies the precise underlying logic: because bearer debentures lack a formally registered owner and pass strictly by mere delivery, the issuing company physically cannot track ownership and thus must mathematically rely on whoever presents the valid coupon.

sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct because the number of debentures issued is calculated by dividing the total purchase consideration by the net issue price of a single debenture. The debentures possess a face value of ₹ 100 and are strictly issued at a 4% discount, making their issue price ₹ 96 each. Dividing the purchase liability of ₹ 24,00,000 entirely by ₹ 96 reliably yields precisely 25,000 debentures.

Renu agreed to receive interest on this amount as per the provisions of Partnership Act, 1932. The rate at which interest would be paid to Renu is :
sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct because Section 37 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 clearly stipulates that if a retiring partner's remaining dues remain entirely unsettled, they are legally entitled to receive interest exclusively at the strict statutory rate of 6% per annum on the outstanding balance until final payment.

questions.text:
रीहा, मीनू तथा सारा एक साझेदारी फर्म की साझेदार थीं तथा 2:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करती थीं । 1 अप्रैल, 2023 से उन्होंने बराबर-बराबर अनुपात में लाभ विभाजित करने के लिए सहमति दी। उस तिथि को फ़र्म की पुस्तकों में ₹ 50,000 का सामान्य संचय था। यह सहमति हुई कि :
(i) फ़र्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹ 3,00,000 किया जाएगा ।
(ii) सम्पत्तियों के पुनर्मूल्यांकन तथा देयताओं के पुनर्निर्धारण पर लाभ की राशि ₹ 30,000 थी।
फ़र्म की पुस्तकों में उपरोक्त लेन-देनों के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
Reeha, Meenu and Sara were partners in a partnership firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:2:1. With effect from 1st April, 2023, they agreed to share profits and losses equally. On that date, there was a General Reserve of ₹ 50,000 in the books of the firm. It was agreed that:
(i) Goodwill of the firm be valued at ₹ 3,00,000.
(ii) Profit on revaluation of assets and re-assessment of liabilities amounted to ₹ 30,000.
Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of the firm.

key_points: Record journal entry transferring General Reserve entirely to partners in old profit-sharing ratio
Record journal entry distributing the total Revaluation Profit clearly among partners in the old ratio
Calculate Sacrificing and Gaining portions resulting from the ratio change
Record a single adjusting entry to compensate for Goodwill using partners' capital accounts

questions.solution:
Three crucial journal entries must be explicitly recorded. First, the General Reserve is fully distributed. General Reserve Account is debited with ₹ 50,000. Reeha's Capital Account is credited with ₹ 20,000, Meenu's with ₹ 20,000, and Sara's with ₹ 10,000, strictly in their old ratio of 2:2:1. 
Second, the Revaluation Profit must be distributed identically. Revaluation Account is logically debited with ₹ 30,000. Reeha's Capital Account is credited with ₹ 12,000, Meenu's with ₹ 12,000, and Sara's with ₹ 6,000. 
Third, the Goodwill adjustment is executed based on ratio changes. The old ratio was 2/5, 2/5, 1/5 and the new ratio is 1/3, 1/3, 1/3. Thus, Reeha sacrifices 1/15th (2/5 minus 1/3), Meenu sacrifices 1/15th, and Sara gains 2/15th (1/3 minus 1/5). The firm's total goodwill is evaluated at ₹ 3,00,000. Sara's capital account must be robustly debited with ₹ 40,000 (which is 2/15th of 3,00,000) to compensate the others. Consequently, Reeha's Capital Account is credited with ₹ 20,000, and Meenu's Capital Account is credited with ₹ 20,000, flawlessly completing the adjustment.

sub_questions.text_english: Mahesh Ltd. purchased Plant and Machinery from Ish Ltd. for ₹ 4,50,000. ₹ 50,000 was paid by cheque to Ish Ltd. and the balance by issuing 6% debentures of ₹ 100 each at a discount of 20%. Record partial cash payment via bank
Calculate the number of debentures issued considering the precise discount
Record debenture issuance by debiting Vendor and Discount Account, and crediting Debentures Account

sub_questions.solution: In the books of Mahesh Ltd., the first entry strictly records the acquisition. Plant and Machinery Account is debited with ₹ 4,50,000, and Ish Ltd. is credited with ₹ 4,50,000. Next, the partial cheque payment is documented by debiting Ish Ltd. with ₹ 50,000 and crediting the Bank Account with ₹ 50,000. The remaining unpaid balance equals ₹ 4,00,000. This is settled by issuing 6% debentures. With a face value of ₹ 100 and a 20% discount, the net issue price calculates to ₹ 80 per debenture. Dividing ₹ 4,00,000 by ₹ 80 yields exactly 5,000 debentures. Therefore, the final entry debits Ish Ltd. with ₹ 4,00,000, debits the Discount on Issue of Debentures Account with ₹ 1,00,000 (which is 5,000 debentures multiplied by the ₹ 20 discount), and heavily credits the 6% Debentures Account with the total face value of ₹ 5,00,000.

sub_questions.text_english: Manika Ltd. forfeited 500 shares of ₹ 100 each for non-payment of first call of ₹ 20 per share and second and final call of ₹ 25 per share. 250 of these shares were reissued at ₹ 50 per share fully paid up. Pass the Journal Entries for forfeiture and reissue of shares.

key_points: Record forfeiture of fully called up shares, tracking unpaid calls and received amount
Record reissue of subset of shares at a discount using Bank and Share Forfeiture
Calculate the proportionate forfeited profit and transfer it to Capital Reserve

sub_questions.solution:
First, the forfeiture entry is recorded. Because the final call was indeed made, the entire ₹ 100 is explicitly called up. The Share Capital Account is debited with ₹ 50,000. Since the first call of ₹ 20 and final call of ₹ 25 were unpaid, the Calls in Arrears Account (or respective call accounts) is credited with ₹ 22,500. This implies ₹ 55 per share was previously paid. Hence, the Share Forfeiture Account is firmly credited with ₹ 27,500.
During the reissue phase, 250 shares are reissued. The Bank Account is debited with ₹ 12,500 (250 shares multiplied by ₹ 50). To cover the discount given, the Share Forfeiture Account is suitably debited with ₹ 12,500. The Share Capital Account is then securely credited with ₹ 25,000.
Finally, the capital reserve transfer must be precisely calculated. The original forfeited amount attached to the 250 reissued shares specifically is ₹ 13,750. Subtracting the ₹ 12,500 discount utilised during reissue leaves a net profit balance. Consequently, the Share Forfeiture Account is debited with ₹ 1,250 and the Capital Reserve Account is explicitly credited with ₹ 1,250.

sub_questions.text_english:
Aayush and Krish are partners sharing profits and losses equally. They decided to admit Vansh for an equal share in the profits. For this purpose, the goodwill of the firm was to be valued at four years purchase of super profits.

The balance sheet of the firm on 31.3.2023 before admission of Vansh was as follows:
Balance Sheet of Aayush and Krish as on 31.3.2023

| Liabilities | Amount (₹) | Assets | Amount (₹) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Capitals: | | Machinery | 75,000 |
| Aayush | 90,000 | Furniture | 15,000 |
| Krish | 50,000 | 1,40,000 | Stock | 30,000 |
| General Reserve | 20,000 | Debtors | 20,000 |
| Loan | 25,000 | Cash | 50,000 |
| Creditors | 5,000 | | |
| Total | 1,90,000 | Total | 1,90,000 |

The normal rate of return is 12% per annum. Average profit of the firm for the last four years was ₹ 30,000. Calculate Vansh's share of Goodwill.

key_points: Calculate Capital Employed utilizing the Liabilities Approach (Capitals + Reserves) or Assets Approach
Compute the Normal Profit by applying NRR to the Capital Employed
Find Super Profit by subtracting Normal Profit from Average Profit
Evaluate Total Firm Goodwill using the designated years of purchase
Determine the new partner's specific share of that evaluated Goodwill

sub_questions.solution:
First, the firm's Capital Employed must be accurately determined. Using the liabilities approach, we add the existing capital balances and the free reserves: ₹ 1,40,000 (total capitals) plus ₹ 20,000 (General Reserve) precisely equals ₹ 1,60,000. (The loan and creditors represent outside liabilities). 
Next, we calculate the Normal Profit by applying the 12% Normal Rate of Return to the ₹ 1,60,000 Capital Employed, which correctly evaluates to ₹ 19,200. 
The Super Profit is found by meticulously subtracting this Normal Profit from the firm's Average Profit. Thus, ₹ 30,000 minus ₹ 19,200 strictly yields a Super Profit of ₹ 10,800.
Subsequently, the total firm Goodwill is computed on the basis of 4 years' purchase of this Super Profit. Multiplying ₹ 10,800 by 4 evaluates the firm's entire Goodwill to securely be ₹ 43,200. Since Vansh is specifically admitted for an equal one-third share alongside Aayush and Krish, his designated share of the Goodwill is one-third of ₹ 43,200. This perfectly yields Vansh's final share of Goodwill as exactly ₹ 14,400.

sub_questions.text: वरुण, तरुण, अरुण तथा बरुण एक फ़र्म के साझेदार थे तथा 5:3:2:2 के अनुपात में लाभ बाँटते थे । 31 मार्च, 2023 को अरुण सेवानिवृत्त हो गया। वरुण, तरुण तथा बरुण ने भविष्य में लाभ बराबर-बराबर बाँटने का निर्णय लिया। अरुण के सेवानिवृत्त होने पर फ़र्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹9,00,000 किया गया । अपने कार्य को स्पष्टता से दर्शाते हुए, ख्याति खाता खोले बिना ख्याति के लेखांकन के लिए अरुण की सेवानिवृत्ति पर आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टि कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Varun, Tarun, Arun and Barun were partners in a firm sharing profits in the ratio of 5:3:2:2. Arun retired on 31st March, 2023. Varun, Tarun and Barun decided to share future profits equally. On Arun's retirement, Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 9,00,000. Showing your workings clearly, pass the necessary Journal entry for treatment of Goodwill on Arun's retirement without opening goodwill account.

key_points: Calculate the retiring partner's explicit share of the firm's goodwill
Compute the individual gaining/sacrificing ratios accurately for the remaining partners
Recognise that a remaining partner may surprisingly be making a sacrifice instead of gaining
Pass the adjusting journal entry debiting gaining partners and crediting sacrificing/retiring partners directly

sub_questions.solution:
Initially, Arun's direct share in the firm's valued goodwill must be determined. Since his old share was 2/12th, multiplying 2/12 by ₹ 9,00,000 yields exactly ₹ 1,50,000 as his rightful goodwill compensation.
Next, we calculate the gain or sacrifice for the remaining partners by subtracting old shares from their new 1/3rd equal shares. 
For Varun: New (1/3) minus Old (5/12) equals -1/12. A negative result means Varun actually sacrifices 1/12th of his share. He therefore requires compensation of ₹ 75,000 (which is 1/12th of ₹ 9,00,000).
For Tarun: New (1/3) minus Old (3/12) equals 1/12. Tarun evidently gains 1/12th.
For Barun: New (1/3) minus Old (2/12) equals 2/12. Barun visibly gains 2/12th.
Finally, the adjusting entry is recorded. Tarun's Capital Account is debited with ₹ 75,000 (his 1/12th gain), and Barun's Capital Account is heavily debited with ₹ 1,50,000 (his 2/12th gain). Conversely, Arun's Capital Account is credited with his full due of ₹ 1,50,000, and Varun's Capital Account is credited with ₹ 75,000 to fully compensate his sacrifice. This systematically balances the accounting treatment.

questions.text_english: Atul and Gita were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2. Their fixed capitals were ₹ 4,00,000 and ₹ 2,00,000 respectively. After the accounts for the year were prepared, it was noticed that interest on capital @ 6% p.a., as provided in the partnership deed, was not credited to the capital accounts of partners before distribution of profits. Pass the necessary adjusting Journal entry. Show your workings clearly.

key_points: Calculate omitted Interest on Capital for both partners
Determine total omitted expense forming a divisible loss
Distribute that total loss in the old profit sharing ratio
Compute the net effect (debit/credit) and pass entry using CURRENT accounts

questions.solution:
First, the omitted interest on capital must be explicitly calculated. Atul is entitled to 6% of his ₹ 4,00,000 fixed capital, totaling ₹ 24,000. Gita is entitled to 6% of her ₹ 2,00,000 capital, totaling ₹ 12,000. Together, this amounts to a total firm expense of ₹ 36,000 that was mistakenly skipped. 
Because this ₹ 36,000 was instead erroneously distributed as profit, it must now be legally recovered as a firm loss. This loss is distributed in their agreed 3:2 ratio. Atul's share of this loss equates to ₹ 21,600, while Gita's share equates to ₹ 14,400.
Comparing the entitlements against the losses establishes the net effect. Atul should receive a credit of ₹ 24,000 but a debit of ₹ 21,600, resulting in a net credit balance of ₹ 2,400. Gita should receive a credit of ₹ 12,000 but a debit of ₹ 14,400, resulting in a net debit balance of ₹ 2,400. 
Crucially, since the problem states their capitals are 'fixed', the adjusting journal entry must securely route exclusively through their current accounts. Thus, Gita's Current Account is debited with ₹ 2,400 and Atul's Current Account is correspondingly credited with ₹ 2,400.

Ronit Ltd. was registered with an authorised capital of ₹ 75,00,000 divided into 75,000 equity shares of ₹ 100 each. The company invited applications for issuing 45,000 shares. The amount was payable as follows: ₹ 30 per share on application, ₹ 30 per share on allotment, ₹ 25 per share on first call and balance on final call.
Applications were received for 42,000 shares and allotment was made to all the applicants. Charvi, to whom 3,300 shares were allotted, failed to pay both the calls. Her shares were forfeited. Present the share capital in the Balance Sheet of the company as per Schedule III, Part I of the Companies Act, 2013. Also prepare notes to accounts.

key_points: Present Share Capital accurately in the main Balance Sheet format
Detail Authorised Capital securely in Notes to Accounts
Detail Issued Capital properly in Notes to Accounts
Detail Subscribed and fully paid-up capital excluding forfeited shares
Calculate and add the forfeited shares amount accurately

questions.solution:
In the main Balance Sheet of Ronit Ltd., according to Schedule III, Part I of the Companies Act, 2013, an amount of ₹ 40,68,000 is cleanly presented under the primary heading 'Equity and Liabilities', sub-heading 'Shareholders' Funds', exclusively against the line item 'Share Capital'.
To explain this, the detailed Notes to Accounts must be properly prepared. First, the Authorised Capital strictly declares 75,000 equity shares of ₹ 100 each, evaluating to ₹ 75,00,000. Next, the Issued Capital explicitly displays 45,000 equity shares of ₹ 100 each, evaluating to ₹ 45,00,000.
The core calculation lies within the Subscribed Capital. Since the company received applications for only 42,000 shares and later forfeited 3,300 shares held by Charvi, the remaining 'Subscribed and fully paid-up' portion comprises 38,700 shares. Thus, 38,700 equity shares of ₹ 100 each evaluate strictly to ₹ 38,70,000. 
Additionally, the amount successfully received on Charvi's forfeited shares must be securely added. Charvi effectively paid the application and allotment money (₹ 30 plus ₹ 30) making a total of ₹ 60 per share on 3,300 shares. This Share Forfeiture amount firmly equates to ₹ 1,98,000. By diligently summing the ₹ 38,70,000 and the ₹ 1,98,000 forfeited balance, the total finalized share capital precisely comes to ₹ 40,68,000.

Prepare Rohan's Capital Account to be rendered to his executors.

Calculate average profit, value total goodwill, and determine Rohan's specific share
Distribute Rohan's goodwill share to surviving partners in gaining ratio
Calculate Rohan's share of profit up to date of death using the time basis

questions.solution:
To prepare Rohan's Capital Account, we sequentially credit his various entitlements. First, his opening capital balance is explicitly recorded as 'By Balance b/d' at ₹ 3,00,000. Second, the General Reserve of ₹ 18,000 is distributed based on his 1/6th profit share, yielding a credit entry of ₹ 3,000. 
Next, we calculate his goodwill. The average profit of the last three years sums to ₹ 2,70,000 divided by 3, which is ₹ 90,000. This is contributed by Ram and Ravi in their existing 2:3 gaining ratio. Therefore, we credit 'By Ram's Capital A/c' with ₹ 12,000 and 'By Ravi's Capital A/c' with ₹ 18,000.
Finally, the profit until death on September 30 (representing exactly 6 months) is computed. Utilizing the ₹ 90,000 average profit, the calculation is ₹ 90,000 multiplied by 1/2 (for 6 months) multiplied by 1/6 (his share), which cleanly equals ₹ 7,500. This is credited as 'By Profit and Loss Suspense A/c' for ₹ 7,500.

sub_questions.text_english: Lazal Ltd. invited applications for issuing 2,00,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each, at 20% premium. Amount per share was payable as follows: ₹ 5 on application; ₹ 4 (including premium) on allotment; and balance on first and final call. Public applied for 3,20,000 shares, out of which applications for 20,000 shares were rejected and shares were allotted on pro-rata basis to the remaining applications. Kavita, an applicant of 15,000 shares failed to pay allotment and call money. Her shares were forfeited. Pass necessary Journal entries for the above transactions in the books of the company.

key_points: Record receipt of excess application money and handle refunds
Transfer application money and adjust pro-rata excess towards allotment
Calculate Kavita's allotted shares and her specific unpaid allotment considering advance
Record allotment due and actual receipt subtracting unpaid arrears
Record call due and actual receipt subtracting unpaid arrears
Pass comprehensive forfeiture entry splitting capital, unpaid premium, and forfeiture amounts

sub_questions.solution:
For Lazal Ltd., the primary application receipt is documented by debiting the Bank Account and crediting the Share Application Account for ₹ 16,00,000 (calculated from 3,20,000 shares multiplied by ₹ 5). Subsequently, this application money is securely distributed. Share Application Account is debited with ₹ 16,00,000. Share Capital Account receives ₹ 10,00,000 (for 2,00,000 shares). Since 20,000 shares were rejected, ₹ 1,00,000 is directly refunded through a credit to the Bank Account. The excess from the pro-rata category applies to 1,00,000 shares. Thus, ₹ 5,00,000 is transferred by crediting the Share Allotment Account.
When the allotment of ₹ 8,00,000 becomes due (₹ 4,00,000 to capital and ₹ 4,00,000 to securities premium), we must specifically calculate Kavita's default. She applied for 15,000 shares. Based on the 3:2 pro-rata ratio (3,00,000 applicants for 2,00,000 shares), she was allotted precisely 10,000 shares. Her application payment was ₹ 75,000, while her required application money was strictly ₹ 50,000. The excess ₹ 25,000 automatically adjusts towards her allotment due of ₹ 40,000. Her actual unpaid allotment thus firmly evaluates to ₹ 15,000. Total bank receipt on allotment is computed as ₹ 8,00,000 (due) minus ₹ 5,00,000 (advance) minus ₹ 15,000 (Kavita's arrears), culminating at exactly ₹ 2,85,000. The Bank Account is debited, and the Share Allotment Account is credited accordingly.
The final call is made due for ₹ 6,00,000 (2,00,000 shares at ₹ 3). Kavita fails to pay on her 10,000 shares, generating arrears of ₹ 30,000. The bank receives ₹ 5,70,000, safely logged into the accounts.
Finally, Kavita's 10,000 shares are officially forfeited. Since her ₹ 25,000 advance effectively covered her capital due on allotment but left ₹ 15,000 unpaid regarding the premium, the Securities Premium Account must be actively debited with ₹ 15,000 alongside the Share Capital debit of ₹ 1,00,000. Consequently, Calls in Arrears is credited with ₹ 45,000 (allotment and call). Her total paid amount of ₹ 75,000 (application plus advance) is fully captured by crediting the Share Forfeiture Account.

sub_questions.text: चाँद लिमिटेड ने ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 1,00,000 समता अंशों/शेयरों को ₹2 प्रति अंश/शेयर के प्रीमियम पर निर्गमित करने के लिए आवेदन आमंत्रित किए। प्रति अंश/शेयर राशि का भुगतान निम्न प्रकार से देय था : आवेदन पर ₹4 (प्रीमियम सहित), आबंटन पर ₹5 तथा शेष प्रथम एवं अन्तिम याचना पर । 1,80,000 अंशों/शेयरों के लिए आवेदन प्राप्त हुए, जिनमें से 30,000 अंशों/शेयरों के आवेदनों को रद्द कर दिया गया तथा शेष आवेदकों को आनुपातिक आधार पर अंशों/शेयरों का आबंटन कर दिया गया। मानसी जो 5,000 अंशों/शेयरों की धारक थी प्रथम एवं अन्तिम याचना का भुगतान करने में असफल रही तथा उसके अंशों/शेयरों का हरण (Forfeit) कर लिया गया । उपरोक्त लेनदेनों के लिए कम्पनी की पुस्तकों में आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Chand Ltd. invited applications for issuing 1,00,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each at a premium of ₹ 2 per share. The amount per share was payable as follows: ₹ 4 (including premium) on application, ₹ 5 on allotment and balance on first and final call. Applications were received for 1,80,000 shares of which applications for 30,000 shares were rejected and remaining applicants were allotted shares on pro-rata basis. Mansi holding 5,000 shares failed to pay first and final call money and her shares were forfeited. Pass necessary Journal entries for the above transactions in the books of the company.

key_points: Record initial receipt of application money for oversubscribed issue
Transfer application money covering capital, premium, allotment advances, and refunds
Make allotment due and record actual receipts deducting already received advances
Make final call due, calculate Mansi's arrears, and record actual receipt
Record forfeiture of Mansi's shares cleanly ignoring premium since it was fully paid

sub_questions.solution:
For Chand Ltd., the primary application receipt demands debiting the Bank Account and crediting the Share Application Account for ₹ 7,20,000 (derived from 1,80,000 applied shares multiplied by ₹ 4). 
Subsequently, this application money undergoes structured distribution. The Share Application Account is debited with ₹ 7,20,000. Of this, ₹ 2,00,000 transfers securely to Share Capital (1,00,000 shares at ₹ 2) and ₹ 2,00,000 explicitly transfers to Securities Premium. The 30,000 rejected shares demand a refund, so ₹ 1,20,000 is directly credited to the Bank Account. The pro-rata category (1,50,000 applied for 1,00,000 allotted) produces an excess application of 50,000 shares, creating an advance of ₹ 2,00,000. This is safely deposited by crediting the Share Allotment Account.
When the allotment is formally made due, Share Allotment Account is debited and Share Capital is credited with ₹ 5,00,000 (1,00,000 shares at ₹ 5). Because ₹ 2,00,000 was already acquired as an advance, the Bank Account reliably receives the exact remaining balance of ₹ 3,00,000.
The first and final call of ₹ 3 (to strictly make the total face value ₹ 10) is then made due, demanding ₹ 3,00,000. Mansi, holding 5,000 shares, strictly defaults on this specific call. Her arrears explicitly equal ₹ 15,000. The firm collects the remaining funds, debiting the Bank Account with ₹ 2,85,000.

sub_questions.solution:
Several chronological journal entries are formally required upon Chahat's admission. Firstly, Chahat's financial contribution is logged by debiting Cash A/c with ₹ 1,20,000 and correspondingly crediting Chahat's Capital A/c with ₹ 90,000 and Premium for Goodwill A/c with ₹ 30,000. Prina, Qadir and Kian were partners in a firm sharing profits in the ratio of 7:2:1. On 31st March, 2023 their Balance Sheet was as follows:
Balance Sheet of Prina, Qadir and Kian as on 31st March, 2023
| Liabilities | Amount (₹) | Assets | Amount (₹) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Capitals: | | Land | 12,00,000 |
| Prina | 9,60,000 | Building | 9,00,000 |
| Qadir | 8,40,000 | Furniture | 3,60,000 |
| Kian | 9,00,000 | 27,00,000 | Stock | 6,60,000 |
| General Reserve | 3,00,000 | Debtors | 6,00,000 |
| Workmen's compensation Reserve | 5,40,000 | Less: Provision for doubtful debts | 30,000 | 5,70,000 |

| Total | 39,00,000 | Total | 39,00,000 |

On the above date Qadir retired on the following terms:
(i) Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 12,00,000.
(ii) Land was to be appreciated by 30% and building was to be depreciated by ₹ 3,54,000.
(iii) A provision of 6% is to be maintained on debtors.
(iv) Liability for workmen's compensation was determined at ₹ 1,40,000.
(v) Amount payable to Qadir was transferred to his loan account.
(vi) Total capital of the new firm was fixed at ₹ 16,00,000 which will be adjusted according to their new profit ratio by opening current accounts.
Prepare Revaluation Account and Partners' Capital Accounts.

key_points: Prepare Revaluation Account by calculating appreciation on land, depreciation on building and adjusting provision on debtors
Distribute Revaluation outcome to old partners
Allocate unutilized Workmen Compensation Reserve and General Reserve
Provide for Qadir's share of goodwill through Prina and Kian's accounts
Calculate the final balance for Qadir and transfer it systematically to his loan account
Determine exact capital deficiencies or surpluses based on new ratio and adjust using current accounts

sub_questions.solution:
The Revaluation Account is prepared to track structural changes in asset valuation. On the credit side, Land appreciates by 30% generating ₹ 3,60,000. On the debit side, Building depreciates by ₹ 3,54,000. The provision on debtors evaluates to 6% of ₹ 6,00,000, which is ₹ 36,000. Since a ₹ 30,000 provision exists, an additional ₹ 6,000 must be debited. The total debits precisely equal the ₹ 3,60,000 credit, resulting in exactly zero revaluation profit or loss.
For the Partners' Capital Accounts, opening balances are entered. The ₹ 3,00,000 General Reserve is credited strictly in their 7:2:1 ratio: ₹ 2,10,000 for Prina, ₹ 60,000 for Qadir, and ₹ 30,000 for Kian. The Workmen Compensation Reserve stands at ₹ 5,40,000 with a claim of ₹ 1,40,000. The free ₹ 4,00,000 is distributed identically: ₹ 2,80,000 to Prina, ₹ 80,000 to Qadir, and ₹ 40,000 to Kian. 
The firm goodwill is ₹ 12,00,000. Qadir's 2/10th share requires a ₹ 2,40,000 credit. Because the remaining ratio is unchanged at 7:1, Prina's capital bears ₹ 2,10,000 and Kian's bears ₹ 30,000. Following these credits, Qadir's final balance equals his ₹ 8,40,000 opening capital plus ₹ 60,000, ₹ 80,000, and ₹ 2,40,000. This massive ₹ 12,20,000 aggregate is strictly transferred directly into Qadir's Loan Account.
Finally, the remaining capitals undergo realignment. The fixed total new capital is ₹ 16,00,000, shared between Prina and Kian in 7:1. Thus, Prina requires ₹ 14,00,000 and Kian requires ₹ 2,00,000. Prina's current operational balance stands at ₹ 12,40,000, presenting a ₹ 1,60,000 shortfall, while Kian's stands at ₹ 9,40,000, presenting an enormous ₹ 7,40,000 excess. These specific discrepancies are explicitly rectified by opening their Current Accounts.

questions.text_english:
Pass the necessary journal entries for the following transactions on the dissolution of the partnership firm of Tina and Rina after the various assets (other than cash and bank) and external liabilities have been transferred to realisation account:
(i) There was an outstanding bill for repairs for which ₹ 20,000 were paid.
(ii) The firm had stock of ₹ 80,000. Tina took over 50% of the stock at a discount of 20% while the remaining stock was sold off for ₹ 52,000.
(iii) The firm had 100 shares of ₹ 10 each which were taken over by the partners at market value of ₹ 20 per share in their profit sharing ratio of 3:2.
(iv) Realisation expenses of ₹ 4,000 were paid by Rina.
(v) Tina had given a loan of ₹ 40,000 to the firm which was duly paid.
(vi) Rina agreed to pay off her husband's loan of ₹ 10,000 at a discount of 10%.

key_points: Record payment of unrecorded liability through Realisation account
Record asset takeover by partner and cash sale of remaining asset through Realisation account
Record investment takeover by partners in profit sharing ratio
Record expense payment made by partner
Record settlement of partner's distinct loan explicitly outside realisation
Record partner assuming external liability at discounted value

questions.solution:
In the process of firm dissolution, specific events mandate distinct entries. For (i), the payment of an outstanding bill is an unrecorded liability. The Realisation Account is heavily debited with ₹ 20,000 and the Bank Account is credited identically. 
For (ii), the stock treatment breaks into two parts. Half the stock (₹ 40,000) taken by Tina at a 20% discount evaluates strictly to ₹ 32,000. Consequently, Tina's Capital Account is debited with ₹ 32,000. The remaining half is sold for ₹ 52,000, so the Bank Account is debited with ₹ 52,000. The Realisation Account takes a combined credit of ₹ 84,000.
For (iii), the 100 shares at a market price of ₹ 20 represent a ₹ 2,000 total asset. Tina and Rina assume this in their 3:2 ratio. Thus, Tina's Capital Account is debited with ₹ 1,200, Rina's Capital Account is debited with ₹ 800, and Realisation is credited with ₹ 2,000.
For (iv), Rina assuming the ₹ 4,000 expenses requires debiting the Realisation Account and crediting Rina's Capital Account directly with ₹ 4,000.
For (v), a partner's loan is crucially independent of realization. The firm debits Tina's Loan Account and credits the Bank Account explicitly with ₹ 40,000.
Lastly, for (vi), Rina assumes her husband's external loan but purely at a 10% discount, making the obligation ₹ 9,000. The Realisation Account is appropriately debited with ₹ 9,000, creating an equivalent credit explicitly in Rina's Capital Account.

निम्नलिखित परिस्थितियों में अजंता लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन तथा ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन पर बट्टे/हानि को अपलिखित करने के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए :
(i) ₹ 1,000 प्रत्येक के 200, 9% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 10% बट्टे पर किया गया, जिनका शोधन सममूल्य पर किया जाएगा। प्रतिभूति प्रीमियम खाते का शेष ₹ 15,000 है।
(ii) ₹ 1,000 प्रत्येक के 300, 11% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 5% बट्टे पर किया गया, जिनका शोधन 10% प्रीमियम पर किया जाएगा। प्रतिभूति प्रीमियम खाते का शेष ₹ 35,000 है।
questions.text_english:
Pass necessary journal entries relating to issue of debentures and to write off discount/loss on issue of debentures in the books of Ajanta Ltd. in the following cases:
(i) 200, 9% debentures of ₹ 1,000 each are issued at 10% discount and redeemable at par. Balance in Securities Premium account is ₹ 15,000.
(ii) 300, 11% debentures of ₹ 1,000 each are issued at 5% discount and redeemable at a premium of 10%. Balance in Securities Premium account is ₹ 35,000.

key_points: Record issue of debentures at a discount in case (i)
Write off the discount amount utilizing available Securities Premium and Statement of P&L
Record issue of debentures combining issue discount and redemption premium into Loss on Issue in case (ii)
Write off the total accumulated loss utilizing the available Securities Premium and Statement of P&L

questions.solution:
For Ajanta Ltd., case (i) concerns the issuance of debentures strictly at a discount. The total face value is precisely ₹ 2,00,000. With a 10% discount evaluating to ₹ 20,000, the bank receipt is ₹ 1,80,000. The first entry debits the Bank Account and credits the Debenture Application and Allotment Account with ₹ 1,80,000. The second entry moves this balance; Debenture Application and Allotment is debited with ₹ 1,80,000, Discount on Issue of Debentures Account is debited with ₹ 20,000, and the 9% Debentures Account is credited completely with ₹ 2,00,000. To write this discount off, the firm possesses only ₹ 15,000 in Securities Premium. Hence, Securities Premium Account is debited with ₹ 15,000, Statement of Profit and Loss is debited with the ₹ 5,000 shortfall, and Discount on Issue is credited entirely with ₹ 20,000.
Case (ii) presents a dual complication of an issue discount paired with a heavy redemption premium. The 300 debentures hold a face value of ₹ 3,00,000. The 5% issue discount demands ₹ 15,000, resulting in a ₹ 2,85,000 bank receipt. The 10% redemption premium creates an extra ₹ 30,000 liability. The first entry records the receipt: Bank Account Dr to Debenture App and Allotment for ₹ 2,85,000. In the subsequent transfer entry, Debenture Application and Allotment is debited with ₹ 2,85,000. The total combined Loss on Issue of Debentures seamlessly sums the discount and redemption premium, commanding a massive ₹ 45,000 debit. The 11% Debentures Account captures a ₹ 3,00,000 credit, while Premium on Redemption of Debentures Account captures a ₹ 30,000 credit. To effectively write this loss off, the existing ₹ 35,000 Securities Premium is exhausted. The Securities Premium Account is debited with ₹ 35,000, the Statement of Profit and Loss absorbs the remaining ₹ 10,000 debit, and the combined Loss on Issue Account is firmly credited with ₹ 45,000.

questions.text_english: A business has a current ratio of 3:1 and quick ratio of 1.2:1. If working capital is ₹ 1,80,000, calculate total current assets and inventory.

key_points: Formulate Current Assets in terms of Current Liabilities using Current Ratio
Substitute this formulation securely into the Working Capital equation to determine Current Liabilities
Multiply Current Liabilities to effectively solve for Total Current Assets
Formulate Quick Assets using Quick Ratio and calculate their exact numerical value
Subtract Quick Assets reliably from Current Assets to finalize Inventory

questions.solution:
The mathematical calculation heavily relies on standard accounting ratio formulas. The Current Ratio dictates that Current Assets uniquely equal 3 times Current Liabilities (CA = 3CL). The Working Capital formula strictly asserts that Working Capital equals Current Assets minus Current Liabilities. Substituting the former, we get 3CL minus CL, mathematically reducing to 2CL. Consequently, with Working Capital standing at ₹ 1,80,000, the 2CL equates to ₹ 1,80,000, confirming Current Liabilities rigidly equal ₹ 90,000. Total Current Assets are then exactly ₹ 90,000 multiplied by 3, which is ₹ 2,70,000. 
Next, the Quick Ratio implies that Quick Assets equal 1.2 times Current Liabilities. Hence, Quick Assets precisely equal 1.2 multiplied by ₹ 90,000, culminating at ₹ 1,08,000. Finally, Inventory is determined by the fundamental difference between total Current Assets and Quick Assets. Subtracting ₹ 1,08,000 strictly from ₹ 2,70,000 flawlessly identifies the Inventory value as ₹ 1,62,000.

key_points: Determine Net Profit Before Tax using the differential in Statement of Profit and Loss and current year tax provision
Calculate loss on sale of machinery and identify current year depreciation via a ledger account
Recognise amortised goodwill mathematically and add back to operating profit
Analyze working capital changes using differences in inventories, trade receivables, and trade payables
Deduct precise tax paid during the year to find final Cash Flow

questions.solution:
Commencing the calculation, the Net Profit Before Tax rigorously stands as the starting anchor. The visible change in the Statement of Profit and Loss balance evaluates strictly to ₹ 1,00,000 (i.e. ₹ 5,00,000 minus ₹ 4,00,000). To this profit, the explicit current year Provision for Taxation amounting to ₹ 80,000 must be securely added back, culminating in a stable Net Profit Before Tax of ₹ 1,80,000.
Progressing next to non-cash and non-operating adjustments. The machine's actual book value effectively was ₹ 2,55,000 (cost ₹ 3,00,000 minus accumulated depreciation ₹ 45,000). By selling it merely for ₹ 1,35,000, the firm suffered an absolute loss of ₹ 1,20,000, which is added back. Goodwill drastically fell from ₹ 2,00,000 to ₹ 1,40,000, representing an amortisation expense of ₹ 60,000 to be safely added back. Furthermore, an Accumulated Depreciation Account must be drafted. The account opens with a ₹ 1,00,000 credit balance. The ₹ 45,000 depreciation accumulated solely on the sold machine is definitively debited. It eventually closes with a ₹ 2,50,000 credit balance. The resulting balancing figure on the credit side yields the massive current year depreciation expense, which mathematically equals ₹ 1,95,000. Adding these expenses (₹ 1,20,000 plus ₹ 60,000 plus ₹ 1,95,000) to the profit generates an Operating Profit Before Working Capital Changes exactly equaling ₹ 5,55,000.
Shifting focus to working capital changes. Inventories undesirably increased by ₹ 50,000, signaling a cash outflow to be deducted. Trade Receivables significantly increased by ₹ 2,00,000, marking another heavy deduction. On a positive note, Trade Payables reliably increased by ₹ 40,000, signifying a cash inflow to be smoothly added. Reconciling these adjustments (₹ 5,55,000 minus ₹ 50,000 minus ₹ 2,00,000 plus ₹ 40,000) leaves exactly ₹ 3,45,000 as cash generated purely from operations.
The final phase deducts income tax paid. Assuming the previous year's full provision was entirely paid, ₹ 60,000 is directly subtracted. Ultimately, subtracting this ₹ 60,000 logically leaves a pristine ₹ 2,85,000, precisely representing the Net Cash Inflow from Operating Activities.
